newsitem.title: USA: Continental, Boeing in sole-supply talk - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Continental, Boeing in sole-supply talk - WSJ.

text.p: Continental Airlines is in talks with Boeing Co to buy its planes exclusively from Boeing, the Wall Street Journal said in Monday's electronic edition.

Continental Chairman Gordon Bethune was quoted as saying in an interview that he had asked Boeing officials to give him an aircraft-contract proposal which would be based on Continental's pact to buy all its planes from Boeing in the coming decades, the newspaper said.
Boeing and Continental have begun preliminary negotiations which Bethune expects will lead to a formal offer from Boeing, the Journal said.

Boeing already has sole supplier agreements with Delta Air Lines and AMR Corp's American Airlines. The Paper said Boeing offers discounts to secure such agreements. According to people familiar with the matter, Boeing agreed, in Delta's case, to lower prices retroactively on some planes which had already been ordered, the Journal said.
Continental is looking to replace 27 McDonnell Douglas Corp DC-10 jetliners and grow its fleet's medium-capacity segment, the paper said.
Neither company was immediately available for comment.
